culture.title: The Kurt Vonnegut Museum and Library
culture.description: A small downtown museum for the city's most famous writer, holding his Smith-Corona typewriter, his Purple Heart and his rejection letters, and running a free banned-books programme.
culture.bonus: Type something on a real typewriter before you leave.

culture.title: The Madam Walker Legacy Center
culture.description: A 1927 African and Egyptian art deco theatre built by the company of Madam C.J. Walker, America's first self-made female millionaire, restored and programming again on Indiana Avenue.
culture.bonus: Look up at the ceiling of the theatre before you look at the stage.

culture.title: An Afternoon at Newfields
culture.description: One of the largest encyclopedic art museums in the country, wrapped in 152 acres of garden and grounds, with a Lilly House estate at the top of the hill.
culture.bonus: Find the Robert Indiana LOVE sculpture and then go and find a work you would rather own.

culture.title: The Reimagined IMS Museum
culture.description: An $89 million rebuild reopened this museum inside the Speedway oval with ten galleries of racing history, and TIME named it one of the World's Greatest Places for 2026.
culture.bonus: Find the oldest car in the building and work out how anyone survived driving it.

culture.title: Climb the Soldiers' and Sailors' Monument
culture.description: The obelisk at the centre of Monument Circle is nearly as tall as the Statue of Liberty, and you can climb 331 steps inside it to a viewing balcony at the top.
culture.bonus: Take all 331 steps rather than the lift, and look at the Circle from directly above it.

culture.title: The Eiteljorg Museum
culture.description: One of only two museums east of the Mississippi holding both Native American and Western American art, in a southwestern-styled building in White River State Park.
culture.bonus: Spend as long in the contemporary Native art galleries as in the historic ones.

culture.title: Indianapolis Symphony at Hilbert Circle Theatre
culture.description: A 1916 theatre right on Monument Circle, converted into a concert hall and home to one of the oldest orchestras in the country, with the monument lit up outside afterwards.
culture.bonus: Walk a full lap of Monument Circle after the concert before you go anywhere else.

culture.title: The Indiana State Museum
culture.description: A purpose-built museum on the canal covering the state from the ice sheets forward, with a limestone-clad exterior that is itself a catalogue of Indiana geology.
culture.bonus: Find the county marker for a county you have actually driven through.

social.title: Race-Town Pints at Daredevil Brewing
social.description: A brewery in the town of Speedway itself, a few blocks from the Brickyard, where the taproom fills with people who have just walked off the Main Street strip.
social.bonus: Walk from the Speedway gates to the taproom rather than driving between them.

social.title: Pinball and Pints at Sun King
social.description: The brewery that made Indianapolis a beer city, with twenty-five-plus taps, a games corner full of pinball and enough floor space to lose a group in.
social.bonus: Win a pinball game while holding a full pint in your other hand.

social.title: Cocktails at The Ball & Biscuit
social.description: A narrow, dark, brick-walled bar on Mass Ave doing serious cocktails with a jukebox loud enough that you have to lean in to talk.
social.bonus: Tell the bartender two spirits you like and let them build something off-menu.

social.title: A Show at The Vogue
social.description: A 1938 Broad Ripple movie house turned music venue, restored, with a sightline from almost anywhere on the floor and a bar along the whole back wall.
social.bonus: Stay for the encore even if you have an early start.

social.title: Beer Garden at the Rathskeller
social.description: A vaulted German beer hall in the basement of the 1894 Athenaeum, with a tree-shaded outdoor biergarten and a stage that runs live music all summer.
social.bonus: Order a liter and stay for whichever band is on, sight unseen.

social.title: Duckpin Bowling at Atomic Bowl
social.description: Two vintage duckpin alleys in the same Fountain Square theatre building — 1950s neon in the basement, 1930s decor on the fourth floor, squat pins and a ball with no holes.
social.bonus: Play one game in the basement and one on the fourth floor, and pick which decade you prefer.

social.title: Live Music at HI-FI Indy
social.description: A small, loud room in the Fountain Square Murphy building booking touring indie and local acts, with an outdoor annex stage for the bigger nights.
social.bonus: Get to the front and stay there for the whole headline set.

social.title: Tasting Room at Hotel Tango
social.description: America's first combat-disabled, veteran-owned distillery, pouring its own gin, vodka and whiskey out of a Fletcher Place tasting room with a big open courtyard.
social.bonus: Order the flight and pick a favourite before you look at which one it was.

social.title: Indians Game at Victory Field
social.description: Routinely called the best minor league ballpark in America — a grass berm in the outfield, the skyline directly over the scoreboard, and tickets that cost almost nothing.
social.bonus: Watch at least three innings from the outfield lawn instead of a seat.

social.title: Patio Pints at Metazoa
social.description: A pet-friendly brewery just north of Fountain Square that gives five per cent of profits to animal charities, with garage doors that roll up onto a skyline-facing patio.
social.bonus: Bring a dog, or befriend someone else's.

social.title: Colts Sunday at Lucas Oil Stadium
social.description: Sixty-seven thousand people under a retractable roof with a window wall that opens onto the downtown skyline, and the whole of Georgia Street to spill into afterwards.
social.bonus: Go on a day the roof and the north window are both open.

social.title: Pacers Night at Gainbridge Fieldhouse
social.description: A basketball-first arena in a state that treats the game as religion — steep, loud, and widely rated the best place to watch an NBA game in the country.
social.bonus: Get there for warm-ups and stay standing for the whole fourth quarter.

8ball.title: The Circle to the Bricks
8ball.description: Start at the centre of Monument Circle. Get yourself to the Speedway gates six miles away without driving a car — bike, bus, scooter, your own legs, or any combination.
8ball.bonus: Do the whole thing without a rideshare, and eat something in Speedway before you head back.

8ball.title: The Tenderloin Hunt
8ball.description: Indiana's state sandwich is served in hundreds of bars and nobody agrees where it is best. Go to one you have never been to and order it without reading a review first.
8ball.bonus: Rank it out of ten before you leave, and text the score to someone who will argue.

adventure.title: Bike the Full Indianapolis Cultural Trail
adventure.description: Eight miles of protected downtown path linking five cultural districts, studded with public art and built well enough that other cities send delegations to look at it.
adventure.bonus: Ride the whole loop and photograph every piece of public art you pass.

adventure.title: Hit the Bays at Topgolf Fishers
adventure.description: Climate-controlled tiered bays, microchipped balls that keep their own score, and a food and drink menu that makes being bad at golf irrelevant.
adventure.bonus: Win a full game against someone who plays real golf.

adventure.title: Hike the Ridges of Eagle Creek Park
adventure.description: Nearly 4,000 acres and a 1,400-acre lake inside the city limits — one of the largest municipal parks in the country, with enough trail to lose an afternoon in.
adventure.bonus: Get far enough from the car park that you cannot hear traffic at all.

adventure.title: Climb the Ladders of Turkey Run
adventure.description: Ninety minutes west of the city, sandstone gorges cut so deep that the state park bolts wooden ladders into them and you scramble through creek beds to get anywhere.
adventure.bonus: Do Trail 3 through the Punch Bowl and accept that your shoes are going to get wet.

adventure.title: Boulder the Walls at North Mass Boulder
adventure.description: A 55,000-square-foot bouldering gym on the near east side with no ropes, a sauna, a fourteen-tap mezzanine bar and a cafe — built to be hung around in, not just climbed.
adventure.bonus: Send a problem two grades above your warm-up, then earn a pint on the mezzanine.

adventure.title: Find the Ruins at Holliday Park
adventure.description: The salvaged facade of a demolished New York skyscraper rebuilt as a folly in the woods above the White River, with three carved figures still staring out of it.
adventure.bonus: Work out what the three statues are meant to represent before you read the plaque.

adventure.title: Kayak the Coves of Geist Reservoir
adventure.description: Eighteen hundred acres of water north-east of the city, busy with boats in the middle and completely still in the coves at either end.
adventure.bonus: Get on the water before nine and beat the wake boats to the quiet water.

adventure.title: Treetop Course at Go Ape, Eagle Creek
adventure.description: A high ropes course strung through the canopy at Eagle Creek — rope bridges, Tarzan swings and ziplines out over the woods, two to three hours of it.
adventure.bonus: Take the Tarzan swing without pausing at the platform.

adventure.title: An Afternoon in White River State Park
adventure.description: A 250-acre park in the middle of downtown holding the zoo, three museums, a ballpark and an amphitheatre, all walkable from one another.
adventure.bonus: Do three separate things inside the park without getting in a car.

adventure.title: Paddle the Central Canal
adventure.description: A flat, three-mile downtown canal you can kayak or pedal-boat straight through the middle of the city, past the zoo and the museums.
adventure.bonus: Paddle the full length without touching either wall.

adventure.title: Kiss the Bricks on an IMS Track Tour
adventure.description: Get driven out onto the two-and-a-half-mile oval, stand on the original yard of bricks at the start-finish line, and kneel down and kiss them like a winner.
adventure.bonus: Actually kiss the bricks. Photograph proof or it does not count.

adventure.title: Walk the Earthworks at Mounds State Park
adventure.description: Ten ceremonial earthworks built by the Adena people around 160 BC, including a Great Mound aligned to the solstice, on a bluff above the White River.
adventure.bonus: Stand in the centre of the Great Mound and work out which way it points.

adventure.title: Trail Run Fort Harrison State Park
adventure.description: A decommissioned army post turned state park on the north-east edge of the city, with hardwood ravine trails and brick officers' quarters still standing along them.
adventure.bonus: Run the Lawrence Creek Trail without walking any of the hills.

adventure.title: Ride the Major Taylor Velodrome
adventure.description: A banked outdoor track named for the Indianapolis-born Black cyclist who became world champion in 1899, with open sessions and loaner track bikes for beginners.
adventure.bonus: Get high enough up the banking that you feel the bike hold itself there.

adventure.title: Ride the Monon North from Broad Ripple
adventure.description: A rail-trail on the old Monon line running north out of Broad Ripple through Carmel, flat and shaded and lined with places to stop.
adventure.bonus: Ride as far as the Carmel Arts District and get a coffee before turning back.

adventure.title: Walk the Plains at the Indianapolis Zoo
adventure.description: The only institution in the country accredited as a zoo, an aquarium and a botanical garden at once, with an orangutan centre where the apes travel overhead on cables.
adventure.bonus: Wait at the Hutan Trail until an orangutan crosses directly above your head.

foodie.title: Etouffee at Yats on Mass Ave
foodie.description: Cajun and Creole out of a chalkboard menu with about six things on it, ladled over rice with a slice of buttered bread, for less money than it has any right to cost.
foodie.bonus: Order whatever is at the top of the chalkboard without reading the rest.

foodie.title: Breakfast at Café Patachou
foodie.description: The student union for adults, as it calls itself — a scratch-kitchen breakfast institution since 1989 that put Indianapolis brunch on the map.
foodie.bonus: Order the broken yolk sandwich and do not modify it.

foodie.title: Cafeteria Line at Shapiro's Delicatessen
foodie.description: A Jewish deli running since 1905, still served cafeteria-style: you slide a tray down the rail and point at the corned beef being carved in front of you.
foodie.bonus: Order a slice of cake at the start of the line like the regulars do, not the end.

foodie.title: Dinner at 9th Street Bistro
foodie.description: A small, ambitious neighbourhood bistro that landed on Indianapolis Monthly's Best Restaurants list for 2026 — the reservation locals are currently chasing.
foodie.bonus: Book it far enough ahead that you have to plan the rest of the day around it.

foodie.title: Breaded Pork Tenderloin at Workingman's Friend
foodie.description: A 1918 Haughville tavern serving Indiana's state sandwich — a pounded pork tenderloin overhanging the bun by two inches on every side — to a room that has not changed in decades.
foodie.bonus: Finish the whole tenderloin, overhang included, without cutting it up.

foodie.title: The Changing Menu at Beholder
foodie.description: Jonathan Brooks' dim room in Windsor Park, where the menu rewrites itself constantly and nothing is off the table — the most interesting cooking in the city.
foodie.bonus: Order the dish on the menu you understand least.

foodie.title: Build a Board at Goose the Market
foodie.description: A butcher, cheesemonger and sandwich counter in Fall Creek Place, with a basement wine bar underneath it for eating what you just bought upstairs.
foodie.bonus: Let the counter pick all three cheeses without telling them what you like.

foodie.title: Seasonal Plates at Tinker Street
foodie.description: A converted house on East 16th doing precise, seasonal, vegetable-forward cooking in a dining room that feels like eating at someone's very good home.
foodie.bonus: Order two vegetable dishes instead of a main and see if you miss it.

foodie.title: Dinner at Bluebeard
foodie.description: A converted 1924 warehouse in Fletcher Place doing Italian-leaning farm-to-table cooking, with a bread programme good enough to be its own business next door.
foodie.bonus: Order whatever the server says the kitchen is most pleased with tonight.

foodie.title: A Dozen Yeast Donuts at Long's Bakery
foodie.description: A 1955 bakery that sells glazed yeast donuts still warm, by the dozen, cash only, to a queue that forms before six in the morning.
foodie.bonus: Bring cash, buy a dozen, and give at least half of them away.

foodie.title: The Shrimp Cocktail at St. Elmo Steak House
foodie.description: A downtown steakhouse in its original room since 1902, famous less for the beef than for a shrimp cocktail whose horseradish is ground fresh daily and genuinely hurts.
foodie.bonus: Eat a whole shrimp with a full load of the cocktail sauce and do not reach for water.

foodie.title: Warm Loaf from Amelia's
foodie.description: The bakery Bluebeard built next door to itself, turning out sourdough and pastries from the same kitchen team, straight out of the oven onto the counter.
foodie.bonus: Buy a loaf, tear the end off outside, and eat it before you get home.

chill.title: Holcomb Gardens on a Weekday Morning
chill.description: A formal garden and canal walk on the Butler University campus — twenty acres of allee, fountain and woodland that almost nobody outside the university uses.
chill.bonus: Walk the full length of the allee to the fountain without stopping.

chill.title: The Nature Center at Holliday Park
chill.description: A quiet nature centre and rock garden above the White River, with a raptor enclosure and enough shaded bench to spend a whole slow afternoon on.
chill.bonus: Sit in the rock garden for twenty minutes without getting up.

chill.title: Canal Walk at Dusk
chill.description: Three miles of downtown canal lined with walkways, footbridges and war memorials, and best walked in the half hour after the lights come on.
chill.bonus: Walk the whole thing end to end and count the bridges.

chill.title: Riverside Afternoon in Broad Ripple Park
chill.description: A big open park on the White River at the top of the Monon, with lawn, river frontage and the whole of Broad Ripple village to walk into afterwards.
chill.bonus: Walk from the park into the village and find somewhere you have never eaten.

chill.title: An Hour in the White River Gardens
chill.description: Three acres of formal garden and a glass conservatory beside the zoo, with a seasonal butterfly house you stand inside while they land on you.
chill.bonus: Stay still in the butterfly house until one lands on you.

chill.title: Wander the 100 Acres at Newfields
chill.description: A hundred acres of woodland, wetland and lake behind the art museum, used as a free outdoor gallery for large-scale commissioned work — including a boat you can sit in on the water.
chill.bonus: Find Funky Bones and lie down in it.

chill.title: Gallery Floors of the Murphy Building
chill.description: A former Fountain Square department store now stacked with artist studios and small galleries, quiet on a weekday and open to anyone who wanders in.
chill.bonus: Knock on one open studio door and ask the artist what they are working on.

chill.title: Read in the Central Library Atrium
chill.description: A 1917 Greek Revival library with a six-storey glass atrium bolted onto the back of it, and a top-floor reading room looking straight down at the skyline.
chill.bonus: Get to the sixth floor and read for an hour facing the window.

chill.title: Walk to the High Point of Crown Hill
chill.description: The third-largest cemetery in the country, an arboretum in its own right, with James Whitcomb Riley buried on the highest natural point in the city and a full skyline view from it.
chill.bonus: Climb to Riley's grave and find the skyline view before you look at the map.

chill.title: The Reopened Sunken Garden at Garfield Park
chill.description: Three years of restoration work brought the historic Sunken Garden fountains back in June 2026, and they now run with new colour lighting after dark beside the 1916 conservatory.
chill.bonus: Stay past sundown for the lights, then go into the conservatory palm house.
